import pandas as pd

# List all source file paths
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_86/training_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_86/training_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_86/training_2.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_86/training_3.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_86/training_4.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_86/training_5.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_86/training_6.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_86/training_7.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_86/training_8.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_86/training_9.csv"
]

# Read all source CSV files into a list of DataFrames
dfs = []
for file_path in source_files:
    df = pd.read_csv(file_path, index_col=0)
    # Ensure columns are exactly as target schema and types are consistent
    df = df[['admit', 'gre', 'gpa', 'prestige']].copy()
    # Convert types explicitly to match target schema
    df['admit'] = df['admit'].astype(int)
    df['gre'] = df['gre'].astype(int)
    df['gpa'] = df['gpa'].astype(float)
    df['prestige'] = df['prestige'].astype(int)
    dfs.append(df)

# Since all source tables have the exact same schema as the target,
# we perform a union (concatenation) of all source tables
target_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

# Write the combined DataFrame to the target CSV file
target_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_86/target_multisource_cot.csv", index=False)
